classification.difficultyReason: Infer the cylindrical container's radius and height from two fitted spheres.

content.prompt:
Two identical spheres fit exactly inside a cylindrical container, as shown.

The diameter of each sphere is 12 cm.

What is the volume of the cylindrical container, to the nearest cubic centimetre?

spec.description: Two unshaded equal spheres stacked inside an upright cylinder. The spheres touch each other, the side boundaries and the top and bottom levels. Decorative grey shading is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Container diameter equals one sphere diameter; container height equals two sphere diameters.
spec.answerVisibility: No derived dimensions or answers appear.

answer.worked:
The cylinder has radius $12\div2=6\text{ cm}$ and height $2\times12=24\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi r^{2}h\\&=\pi\times6^{2}\times24\\&=864\pi\\&\approx2714\text{ cm}^{3}\end{align*}$$
